market_summary: September ISM manufacturing printed 54.5 against 55.0 consensus, but prices paid jumped to 77.9 from 71.1, the highest since May, with new orders 55.3 and employment 52.7. At 10:30 ET the S&P 500 was 7,632 (-0.3%), Nasdaq 26,822 (-0.2%), SOX flat, Micron down about 3% despite record results, VIX 16.7, and the 10-year at 5.32% after a 5.36% high, the most since 2002; October hike odds 38%. Asia: ASX 200 -2.0% to 8,614, its lowest since mid-June, with the Australian 10-year at 5.40%; Nikkei +3.3% and Kospi +2.0% on chips; Stoxx 600 -1.3% at midday. Brent +2.8% to $100.76 and WTI $91.70 as Iran weighs a US ceasefire counterproposal, Washington told France and Germany to release 120m barrels of diesel or face a US export ban, and OPEC+ is expected to hold November targets on Sunday. The Court of International Trade sounded skeptical of the Section 301 tariffs covering 99.4% of imports. Next 48h (AEST): Jefferson 03:30 Fri, Bowman 05:00, Cook 05:30; Tesla Q3 deliveries Fri before the US open (consensus 462k); US September payrolls 22:30 Fri (consensus 162k, unemployment 4.1%); OPEC+ Sunday; ISM services Tue 01:00 AEDT.

AMZN.reason: Down 0.9% an hour into Thursday after closing Wednesday slightly lower, despite Goldman adding it to its conviction list with a $375 target and a 20-year Calvert Cliffs nuclear deal. AWS growing 37% is the thesis; the yield spike is the drag, not the business.

AXOS.reason: Off 2.9% in the first hour with no company news; the whole bank group is being sold as the 10-year pushes past 5.3%. Q1 FY27 results land Oct 29 and nothing has changed in the deposit or credit picture since.

BABA.reason: Up 0.2% Thursday with Hong Kong shut for National Day through Oct 7, so no local tape; the only new flow is class-action filings over alleged military ties and model-distillation claims. Nothing to act on. Watch.

ENPH.reason: Down 3.4% early with no company news, giving back Wednesday's 2.8% gain as higher yields hit residential solar financing again. Citi already cut its target to $37 this week; wait for Q3 numbers before touching it.

FIGR.reason: Down 3.7% early with no company news; the rate-sensitive lenders are all lower with mortgage rates at a cycle high. Home-equity origination is the business and the Kiavi and Sierra moves are intact, so no change.

GOOGL.reason: Down 0.7% Thursday, giving back the 1.5% premarket pop on Gemini 4 Argon as yields rose; JPMorgan kept Overweight and said Argon is what Google needed to re-establish frontier credibility, and the first TPUs went to orbit today. Still add on dips.

LDI.reason: Down 2.7% in the first hour and still below the NYSE compliance threshold, with the 30-year at 7.60% and the 10-year above 5.3% squeezing origination volume further. Keep trimming into any bounce.

META.reason: Flat (-0.02%) Thursday after a 27% September; Muse monetisation is now explicit (fees on savings, subscriptions, 200M small businesses) and Deutsche Bank named it a next-leg AI pick, but the move is already in the price. Hold.

MRVL.reason: Down 1.0% Thursday with the semis fade; BofA put it on its five must-own chips for Q4 with the Oct 6 analyst day and XPU ramp as catalysts. Nothing new on fundamentals until Monday's event. Hold.

MU.reason: Down 3.1% in the first regular session after the record quarter, on margin softness and profit-taking after a 268% year-to-date run rather than on demand; Goldman lifted its target to $1,250 (Neutral), Mizuho to a $1,400 target, Deutsche kept a $1,550 target. Supply tight into 2028, so hold through the chop.

NFLX.reason: Down 2.0% early after Sarandos said Netflix is 'not growing as fast as I want', while Guggenheim raised its target to $80 and kept a Buy. The Oct 20 print decides it; nothing today changes the long thesis.

NVDA.reason: Up 0.6% an hour into Thursday after a 0.9% premarket bid on Micron's read-through; Barclays sees at least $30B of hyperscaler revenue upside and Cantor reiterated a $350 target, but the 10-year at a 2002 high keeps a lid on multiple expansion. Hold.

RKT.reason: Off 1.8% in the first hour as the 10-year sets a two-decade high above 5.3% and 30-year mortgage rates sit above 7.5%. Refi volume cannot recover at these levels, so stay on the sidelines.

TSM.reason: Flat (+0.01%) in New York after a 1.3% gain in Taipei on Micron's read-through; Bloomberg says TSMC is weighing a multi-fab Texas campus at $20B+ per fab if the 35% CHIPS credit is renewed, with North America over 75% of wafer revenue. Capacity keeps selling out. Add.

STRIPE.reason: No new round or tender; the newsroom's latest items are the Sept 30 Parafin acquisition and OUSD stablecoin launch, both already covered. Mark stays at the last tender.

OPENAI.reason: No closed round reported Thursday; the $30B raise at a $1.4T valuation remains at the talks stage per Sept 29-30 reports, and nothing new surfaced on the FTC demands or the Australian Senate inquiry. Mark unchanged until a round closes.

headlines: US 10-year hit 5.34%, highest since 2002, after ISM prices paid jumped to 77.9; rate-sensitive holdings fell 2-4% early Thursday.
Micron down 3% in its first session after the beat; targets raised at Goldman, Mizuho and Deutsche but the margin guide caps it.
BYD September sales 463,561, up 17% year on year and the best month of 2026; overseas guidance raised to 1.9-2.0m.
ASX 200 fell 2.0% to its lowest since June as Australian yields hit 5.40%; Nikkei +3.3% on chip names.
Amazon signed a 20-year nuclear deal for Calvert Cliffs and joined Goldman's conviction list; Brent back above $100.
Tonight AEST: Fed's Jefferson 03:30, Bowman 05:00; US payrolls and Tesla Q3 deliveries Friday night.
